Undergraduate study

MBBS at SVS

From foundational sciences to clinical learning and community experience.

Medical College

Medical CollegeMBBSMD/MSDepartments & HODsLibrary & FacilitiesLeadershipCommitteesStudent GuideStudent SupportTeaching HospitalContactDisclosures & Approvals

The undergraduate course

SVS Medical College began MBBS teaching in 1999. Confirm the current seat matrix and counselling information for the year you are applying.

How learning is organised

The course follows competency-based medical education: a foundation course, subject teaching, practical work, clinical postings, electives and assessment. Communication, professional ethics and patient dignity run through the course.

Your first steps

The foundation course introduces orientation, basic first aid and life support, professional development, language and computer skills, community visits and extracurricular activity. The skills laboratory gives students a place to practise with mannequins and task trainers before patient contact.

Community learning

The Family Adoption Programme follows households through repeated field visits. Students learn to understand family health, living conditions and community needs, with training connected to the rural and urban health centres.

Attendance and assessment

Students need at least 75% theory attendance and 80% practical or clinical attendance in each subject. Internal assessment, documented competencies and the rules applicable to your admission batch also matter. Ask the academic office for the current calendar and full examination rules.
